items.title: Chink Martin Interview, 1966-10-19
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Dr. Tishner's antiseptic' as a brand of antiseptic carried by a clarinet player in George Lewis's band, but does not indicate any personal relationship with the person Dr. Tishner.

ctx.x: Al, just let me digress one moment. Al Rose told me something the other night. You know how much these Japanese boys over here, how much they imitate the George Lewis band. And that clarinet player thinks George, of course, is the most wonderful thing in the world. And just to show you how far imitation can go sometimes, he had a bottle of Dr. Tishner's antiseptic, you know, in his clarinet case. And somebody asked him, why in the world are you carrying a bottle of Dr. Tishner's in your clarinet case? What's it…

No, we're going right back to where we started from. Now we're speaking about rhythm, tempo, kick, swing. You understand? Dr. Tishner's antiseptic. Now, the people, intelligent people are broad-minded. It's only but the ignorant people that never sits down to try to figure this out. But if the intelligent people, if they just sit down and figure this out for themselves, they're going to find out that I'm telling you the truth. Dr. Tishner's antiseptic. Now, you can learn a poison music, right? Can you learn a…
Dr. Tishner's antiseptic. Well, if you get them to think about it, they can improve, I think.
